frs_sections.title: OVERVIEW AND ARCHITECTURE
frs_sections.content:
SpaceWire is organized as a layered set of protocol levels, in the manner of a
protocol stack. From the lowest to the highest, the levels are:

  - Physical level: connectors, cables, cable assemblies, and printed circuit
    board tracks.
  - Signal level: signal encoding, signal voltage levels, noise margins, and
    data signalling rates. SpaceWire uses LVDS and Data-Strobe (DS) encoding.
  - Character level: data characters and control characters that are passed
    along a link.
  - Exchange level: the protocol for link initialization, flow control, link
    error detection, and link error recovery. The exchange level holds the
    link state machine.
  - Packet level: how data is split up into packets for transfer from source
    to destination across a link or network.

frs_sections.title: CHARACTER LEVEL
frs_sections.content:
There are two types of character in SpaceWire: data characters and control
characters.

A data character is ten bits long and contains:
  - a parity bit (odd parity, covering the previous parity and following bits),
  - a data-control flag bit (set to 0 to indicate a data character),
  - eight bits of data, transmitted least-significant bit first.

A control character is four bits long and contains:
  - a parity bit,
  - a data-control flag bit (set to 1 to indicate a control character),
  - two control bits that select one of four control codes.

The four control characters are:
  - FCT — Flow Control Token. Used for flow control; signals that the receiver
    has room for a further eight N-Chars (one credit unit of eight characters).
  - EOP — End of Packet (Normal end of packet). Marks …

frs_sections.title: PACKET LEVEL
frs_sections.content:
Data is transferred across a SpaceWire link or network in packets. A SpaceWire
packet has the form:

    <Destination Address> <Cargo> <End of Packet Marker>

  - Destination Address — zero or more data characters at the start of the
    packet that determine the route the packet takes to its destination. The
    address may be a path address (a sequence of output port numbers, each
    consumed by a router as the packet passes through), a logical address (a
    single byte identifying the destination node, used with routing tables), or
    a combination (regional logical addressing).
  - Cargo — the data to be transferred (any number of data characters).
  - End of Packet Marker — EOP for a normal end of packet, or EEP for an error
    end of packet.

frs_sections.title: KEY PARAMETERS SUMMARY
frs_sections.content:
- Standard:                ECSS-E-ST-50-12C (SpaceWire — Links, Nodes,
                             Routers and Networks)
  - Signalling:              LVDS (ANSI/TIA/EIA-644), differential
  - Encoding:                Data-Strobe (DS); Clock = Data XOR Strobe
  - Signals per direction:   2 (Data and Strobe), each a differential pair
  - Differential pairs:      4 per bidirectional link (8 wires)
  - Duplex:                  full-duplex, bidirectional, point-to-point
  - Data signalling rate:    2 Mbps to 200+ Mbps (default 10 Mbit/s at reset)
  - Data character:          10 bits (parity + data-control flag + 8 data bits)
  - Control character:       4 bits (parity + data-control flag + 2 control bits)
  - Control characters:      FCT, EOP, EEP, ESC

protocol_overview.type: High-speed, bidirectional, full-duplex, point-to-point serial spacecraft-onboard data link (and the routers / networks built from them). LVDS signalling with Data-Strobe (DS) encoding; layered Physical/Signal/Character/Exchange/Packet/Network. Standardized as ECSS-E-ST-50-12C.
protocol_overview.duplex: Full-duplex, bidirectional: each direction carries an independent Data (D) and Strobe (S) LVDS pair, so data flows both ways simultaneously.
protocol_overview.encoding: Data-Strobe (DS) encoding over LVDS: the Strobe signal changes whenever the Data signal does not, so exactly one of the two signals changes per bit and the clock is recovered as Clock = Data XOR Strobe. Characters carry odd parity.
protocol_overview.modulation: LVDS differential on Data (D+/D-) and Strobe (S+/S-) in each direction.
protocol_overview.topology: node <-> link <-> node / router; routers forward packets by wormhole routing into a SpaceWire network.

compliance_requirements: LVDS signalling with Data-Strobe (DS) encoding; clock = Data XOR Strobe; four differential pairs per bidirectional link.
10-bit data characters and 4-bit control characters; FCT/EOP/EEP/ESC; NULL (ESC+FCT) and Time-Code (ESC + data character); odd parity.
Exchange-level state machine ErrorReset -> ErrorWait -> Ready -> Started -> Connecting -> Run.
Credit-based flow control: one FCT grants eight N-Chars; max 56 outstanding.
Packets <destination address><cargo><EOP/EEP>; wormhole routing; path / logical / regional-logical addressing; group adaptive routing; configuration port (port 0).
Link error detection (disconnect / parity / escape / credit) with ErrorReset recovery.

functional_requirements.text: A SpaceWire link signals over LVDS (ANSI/TIA/EIA-644) using Data-Strobe (DS) encoding: a Data signal and a Strobe signal per direction, each a differential pair, so the clock is recovered as Data XOR Strobe and only one of D/S changes per bit.
A bidirectional full-duplex link uses four LVDS differential pairs (eight wires): Data and Strobe in each direction; there is no separately forwarded clock wire.
Links operate from 2 Mbps to over 200 Mbps; the default data signalling rate after reset is 10 Mbit/s.
The character level defines 10-bit data characters (parity + data-control flag + 8 data bits, LSB first) and 4-bit control characters (parity + data-control flag + 2 control bits).
The four control characters are FCT (Flow Control Token), EOP (End of Packet), EEP (Error End of Packet), and ESC (Escape); ESC+FCT forms NULL and ESC+data-character forms a Time-Code.

The exchange level runs a link initialization state machine ErrorReset -> ErrorWait -> Ready -> Started -> Connecting -> Run; both ends synchronize by exchanging NULLs (link connected) and FCTs (credit available).
Flow control is credit-based: each FCT received grants permission to send eight further N-Chars; up to seven FCTs (56 N-Chars) may be outstanding, bounded by the receive buffer.
Data is transferred in packets of the form <destination address><cargo><EOP or EEP>; packets are of arbitrary length and delimited by EOP (normal) or EEP (error).

A SpaceWire network is built from nodes and routing switches; routers forward packets by wormhole routing using path addressing, logical addressing, and regional-logical addressing, with optional group adaptive routing.
A router has a configuration port (port 0) that accesses its configuration registers (routing table, port control/status, error/status) via RMAP or packets to port 0.
Time-Codes (ESC + a data character carrying a 6-bit time value plus two flags) are broadcast by a time master and forwarded by nodes and routers to distribute a synchronized system time.
The exchange level detects disconnect, parity, escape, and credit errors and recovers by returning to ErrorReset and re-running the initialization handshake.

error_response_conditions: Disconnect error — the gap between Data/Strobe transitions exceeds the disconnect timeout (~850 ns); the other end stopped transmitting.
Parity error — the odd parity covering a character fails.
Escape error — an ESC is followed by another ESC or by an EOP/EEP (an invalid escape sequence).
Credit error — an N-Char arrives with no credit granted, or the transmitter sends with no credit.
On any of these errors the link goes to ErrorReset and re-runs the ErrorReset -> ErrorWait -> Ready -> Started -> Connecting -> Run handshake.
